---
title: "rush plot"
---

{{< include ../_setup.qmd >}}

The `plot` command builds a [ggplot2](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/) graphic
from your data. Choose columns with `--x`, `--y`, `--color`, and friends, and a
sensible geom is guessed for you (override it with `--geom`).

## Usage

```bash
rush plot [options] [--] [<file>...]
```

## Geom selection

When both `--x` and `--y` are given, `rush` guesses `geom_point`:

```{bash}
rush plot -n -x bill_length_mm -y body_mass_g penguins.csv
```

When only `--x` is given, `rush` guesses `geom_histogram`:

```{bash}
rush plot -n -x body_mass_g penguins.csv
```

### `--geom` (`-g`)

Override the guessed geom. Any ggplot2 geom suffix works:

```{bash}
rush plot -n -x body_mass_g -g density penguins.csv
```

```{bash}
rush plot -n -x species -y body_mass_g -g boxplot penguins.csv
```

```{bash}
rush plot -n -x bill_length_mm -y body_mass_g -g smooth penguins.csv
```

## Aesthetics

### `--color` (`-c`)

Map a column to the color aesthetic:

```{bash}
rush plot -n -x bill_length_mm -y body_mass_g -c species penguins.csv
```

### `--fill` (`-f`)

Map a column to fill (useful for histograms, bar charts, density plots):

```{bash}
rush plot -n -x body_mass_g -g density -f species --alpha 0.5 penguins.csv
```

### `--alpha` (`-a`)

Map a column to transparency, or use a constant for semi-transparent geoms:

```{bash}
rush plot -n -x bill_length_mm -y body_mass_g --alpha 0.6 penguins.csv
```

### `--size`

Map a column to point size — great for bubble charts:

```{bash}
rush plot -n -x bill_length_mm -y body_mass_g --size flipper_length_mm -c species penguins.csv
```

### `--shape`

Map a column to point shape:

```{bash}
rush plot -n -x bill_length_mm -y body_mass_g --shape sex penguins.csv
```

### `--group`

Group observations for geoms like `geom_line` that connect points:

```{bash}
rush plot -n -x bill_length_mm -y body_mass_g --group species -g line penguins.csv
```

### `--aes`

Pass additional aesthetics as `key=value` pairs:

```{bash}
rush plot -n -x bill_length_mm -y body_mass_g --aes "label=species" -g text penguins.csv
```

## Axis and labels

### `--log`

Log-transform axes. Accepts `x`, `y`, or `xy`:

```{bash}
rush plot -n -x body_mass_g -y bill_length_mm --log x penguins.csv
```

### `--title`, `--xlab`, `--ylab`

Add axis labels and a title:

```{bash}
rush plot -n -x bill_length_mm -y body_mass_g --title "Bill Length vs Body Mass" --xlab "Bill length (mm)" --ylab "Body mass (g)" penguins.csv
```

## Facets

### One-sided formula (facet_wrap)

```{bash}
rush plot -n -x bill_length_mm -y body_mass_g --facets '~ species' penguins.csv
```

### Two-sided formula (facet_grid) + `--margins`

```{bash}
rush plot -n -x bill_length_mm -y body_mass_g --facets 'sex ~ species' --margins penguins.csv
```

## Pre- and post-processing

### `--pre`

Run code before the plot is built. Useful for data transformations:

```{bash}
rush plot -n -x species -y mean_mass --pre 'df <- df |> dplyr::summarise(mean_mass = mean(body_mass_g), .by = species)' -g col penguins.csv
```

### `--post`

Run code after the plot is built. The plot object is available as `p`:

```{bash}
rush plot -n -x bill_length_mm -y body_mass_g --post 'p + ggplot2::theme_minimal() + ggplot2::geom_smooth(method = "lm")' penguins.csv
```

## Saving plots

### `--output` (`-o`)

When `--output` points to a file, the plot is saved (device inferred from extension):

```{bash}
rush plot -x bill_length_mm -y body_mass_g -c species -o scatter.png penguins.csv 2>/dev/null
ls -la scatter.png
rm -f scatter.png
```

### `--width`, `--height`, `--units`, `--dpi`

Control the saved image dimensions and resolution:

```{bash}
rush plot -x bill_length_mm -y body_mass_g -o hires.png --width 10 --height 6 --units in --dpi 150 penguins.csv 2>/dev/null
ls -la hires.png
rm -f hires.png
```

## Reading from stdin

Without a file argument, `plot` reads from standard input:

```{bash}
rush run 'head(df, 50)' penguins.csv | rush plot -n -x bill_length_mm -y body_mass_g -
```

## Multiple files

With multiple files, each is read into `dfs`. Use `--pre` to combine them
into `df` before plotting:

```{bash}
echo "src,x,y
A,1,2
A,2,4
A,3,5" > a.csv
echo "src,x,y
B,1,3
B,2,2
B,3,6" > b.csv
rush plot -n -x x -y y -c src --pre 'df <- dplyr::bind_rows(dfs)' a.csv b.csv
rm -f a.csv b.csv
```

## Help

```{bash}
rush plot -h
```
